title: Backend: watchlist domain model (DB table + migration)
description: User request: there should be watchlists. No watchlist concept exists anywhere in the codebase yet (not in docs/Analyse.md, not in backend/app/db/models.py, not in the frontend). This task adds the persistence layer only, mirroring how portfolio-domain-models preceded api-portfolio-get/add-position: a new ORM model (e.g. WatchlistItemORM — ticker, added_at at minimum; decide whether a per-item note/target field is worth adding now vs. leaving for later as a decisions entry) and an Alembic migration under backend/app/db/migrations, following the same conventions the existing PositionORM/AccountORM/OHLCVCacheORM and their migration(s) already establish. No API endpoints or frontend here — see api-watchlist (depends on this) and frontend-watchlist-page.

checklist.step: Decide the watchlist item's exact fields (ticker + added_at at minimum; consider a target-price or note field) and record as a decisions entry.
Add the ORM model to backend/app/db/models.py, following the existing models' conventions (typed Mapped columns, appropriate primary key/uniqueness on ticker).
Write the Alembic migration under backend/app/db/migrations, mirroring the existing migration(s)' structure.
Test: migration applies cleanly (up) against a fresh DB and the new table matches the ORM model, following the pattern in backend/tests/integration/test_db_migrations.py.

decisions.decision: WatchlistItemORM has exactly two columns: ticker (String, primary key) and added_at (DateTime, not null). No note/target-price field added.
decisions.rationale: Checked both downstream tasks (api-watchlist.json, frontend-watchlist-page.json) for any requirement touching a note or target-price field -- neither mentions one; api-watchlist's whole point is to annotate each watched ticker with its live-computed signal/confidence from the existing signal engine, not a user-entered target. Adding speculative columns now would mean either exposing them through a not-yet-designed API/UI or leaving dead unused columns in the schema, and yet-another migration would be needed the moment a real requirement for them shows up anyway -- so YAGNI wins over guessing at a shape. Also decided to make ticker itself the primary key (String) rather than following PositionORM's synthetic-id-plus-unique-ticker-column pattern: a watchlist is a set of tickers (add once, remove by ticker -- DELETE /api/watchlist/{ticker} in api-watchlist.json operates on ticker directly, mirroring OHLCVCacheORM's natural-key convention), unlike positions where a synthetic id leaves room for multiple lots of the same ticker over time. Considered and rejected the synthetic-id-plus-unique-ticker pattern for cross-table consistency, since there's no use case here for multiple rows per ticker or for referencing a watchlist entry by an opaque id instead of the ticker itself. Documented both choices in a docstring on the model itself so the next task doesn't have to re-derive the reasoning from this file.
